headline: Top gangster ‘Kailla’ Palash dies a week after Rampura shooting
summary: Yeasin Khan Palash, listed as a top criminal, passed away at Evercare Hospital on Saturday after being shot in Dhaka's Rampura.
details: Yeasin Khan Palash, known as “Kailla” Palash and listed as a top gangster, has died. He passed away around 1am on Saturday at Evercare Hospital Bangladesh following a shooting in Dhaka's Rampura.
The incident occurred around 1:45pm on June 12 near his home outside the Bangladesh Television building in Rampura. He was initially rushed to Dhaka Medical College Hospital in critical condition.

caption:
A top-listed gangster has died a week after being shot in the heart of Dhaka.

Yeasin Khan Palash, known as “Kailla” Palash and listed as a top gangster, has died. He passed away around 1am on Saturday at Evercare Hospital Bangladesh following a shooting in Dhaka's Rampura.

The incident occurred around 1:45pm on June 12 near his home outside the Bangladesh Television building in Rampura. He was initially rushed to Dhaka Medical College Hospital in critical condition.

After two days of treatment at DMCH, he was moved to Evercare Hospital on Sunday night as his condition failed to improve, where he eventually succumbed to his injuries.

Palash's wife, Mahmuda Khanam, filed an attempted murder case with Hatirjheel Police Station, describing the shooting as "premeditated" with intent to kill.

The case names fellow gangster Jisan Ahmed Monty as the prime suspect, along with ten other individuals and several unnamed suspects.

Police have since arrested Imam Hossain in Badda, who is alleged to have been the motorcycle rider helping the shooter flee the scene.

Additionally, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) arrested another suspect, Ferdous, and handed him over to police, stating he was present at the scene during the attack.

headline_marked: Tragedy in Mymensingh: [[Schoolboy electrocuted while hanging Brazil flag]]
headline: Tragedy in Mymensingh: Schoolboy electrocuted while hanging Brazil flag
summary: 14-year-old Mahin Sheikh, an 8th-grade student, died after a bamboo pole touched power lines while he was decorating for the World Cup.
details: Mahin Sheikh, a 14-year-old student of Panchbhag Islamia High School, died after being electrocuted in South Harina village of Mymensingh's Gafran Ganj upazila.
The incident occurred on Friday afternoon while Mahin and his cousin, Fahim Sheikh, were climbing a mango tree to hang a Brazil flag in celebration of the World Cup.
According to local sources, the bamboo pole used to hang the flag tilted and touched a nearby rural electricity line, causing Mahin to be severely injured by the electric shock.
Family members and locals rushed to rescue him after hearing Fahim's screams. He was first taken to the Gafran Ganj Upazila Health Complex and then to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital.
Doctors at the emergency department declared Mahin dead on arrival.
Police from the Pagla police station have been informed of the incident and are taking necessary legal steps, according to Officer-in-Charge Aminul Islam.
caption:
A 14-year-old boy's excitement for the World Cup turned into tragedy when he was electrocuted while hanging a Brazil flag.

Mahin Sheikh, a 14-year-old student of Panchbhag Islamia High School, died after being electrocuted in South Harina village of Mymensingh's Gafran Ganj upazila.

The incident occurred on Friday afternoon while Mahin and his cousin, Fahim Sheikh, were climbing a mango tree to hang a Brazil flag in celebration of the World Cup.

According to local sources, the bamboo pole used to hang the flag tilted and touched a nearby rural electricity line, causing Mahin to be severely injured by the electric shock.

Family members and locals rushed to rescue him after hearing Fahim's screams. He was first taken to the Gafran Ganj Upazila Health Complex and then to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital.

Doctors at the emergency department declared Mahin dead on arrival.

Police from the Pagla police station have been informed of the incident and are taking necessary legal steps, according to Officer-in-Charge Aminul Islam.
